Two term sheets on the table, Sergio. Meridian and Nordbank. Which one do we take to the committee?
Meridian's spread is tighter, so it looks cheaper at first. But the tenor is two years shorter, and that is the trade-off.
Good. And what is the deal-breaker for you? There is always one.
The ceiling on drawdowns. Nordbank sets it far lower than our internal benchmark, and that is the one point I need to push back on.
Then push back on the ceiling and leave the spread alone. Our leverage is better this year than it was last year, so use it.

Hi Sergio, it is Marina. A quick note before the call with Nordbank at four. I read both term sheets again last night. Meridian's spread is tighter, about twenty basis points tighter, but their tenor is two years shorter, and that is the trade-off you have to explain to the committee. Please do not open with the spread. Open with the tenor, because that is the point where Nordbank is stronger, and they know it. The ceiling on drawdowns is the real problem. It sits far below our internal benchmark, and for me that is the deal-breaker. So push back on the ceiling, and only on the ceiling. If they raise it to the benchmark, we settle on Nordbank today. If they do not, we go back to Meridian. Talk at four.

Hi Sergio, it is Paulo from the credit desk. One thought on the two term sheets, and then I will let you go. Everybody in this building looks at the spread first, because it is the easiest number to compare. It is also the smallest one. The longer the tenor, the less refinancing risk we carry, and refinancing risk costs us far more than twenty basis points ever will. So my advice is simple. Treat the tenor as the main number and the spread as the second one. The other thing is leverage. Our track record with Nordbank is better this year than it was last year, so you can ask for more than you think. Ask for the ceiling. The worst answer you get is no. Good luck at four.

First, put the two offers side by side and name the numbers you are comparing. Then say which offer is better on each point, and by how much. Next, name the trade-off, because no offer wins on everything. After that, name the one condition you cannot accept. Finally, say which offer you recommend and what you need from the other side.
